summary: Removed the "intro" and "details" pre-email steps, cutting the funnel from 6 to 4 steps, because every extra click before the email field is a drop-off point and reaching the commitment ask sooner is the single biggest lever for signup conversion.

Removed the "verify" step from the funnel, cutting it from 4 steps to 3, because email verification is the single highest-friction drop-off point in signup flows — users who haven't yet experienced the product's value are unlikely to complete an out-of-band verification step.

Replaced the generic welcome headline and passive "learn more" text link with a benefit-driven headline, a prominent styled CTA button labeled "무료로 시작하기 →" (Start for free), and brief social proof — removing the "learn more" detour that was causing drop-off before users even entered the funnel.

Removed the "confirm" step from the funnel, reducing it from 3 steps to 2, because each additional funnel step typically drops 20–40% of users and an email-collection step alone is sufficient to capture a signup.

Added three concrete benefit bullets (automates repetitive tasks, works on all devices, data encrypted) because visitors who don't know what they'll get hesitate to sign up, and specific outcomes reduce that uncertainty more than any amount of "free and easy" reassurance.

Added three concrete benefit bullets (time saved, cross-device sync, no hidden costs) with checkmarks — giving undecided visitors specific, scannable reasons to click through instead of bouncing off a vague description.
